searchText: Does anyone know when the next spec test release will be? the next one would be `alpha.7`, and we are working on getting that together a few key PRs are still in progress curiosity: right now on the network we have 64 committees each consisted of 526 validator. this means that we are aggregating (supposedly) 33664 attestations per slot. correct? if so why not bump down epoch duration to `8` slots? is it the computation or is there something else i am missing? for that specific epoch with an `8` slots duration you would get `33664*8=269312` which is almost half the current active validator set length 64 committees per slot, and yes each committee has something like 526 validators so then 33664 attestations/slot if epochs were shorter, we would have even more attestations/slot to aggregate which is in general one of the more expensive computations we have in the CL there's also the trade-off b/t per-slot, per-block, and per-epoch scope processing nodes have to do; if epochs are shorter you get less amortization > for that specific epoch with an 8 slots duration you would get 33664*8=269312 which is almost half the current active validator set length i think you are starting at the other end of the design space here -- we want the invariant that every validator makes 1 attestation per epoch; otherwise you start getting much more complicated analyses around finality/PoS security which at best is harder to secure, and at worst means we open ourselves up to attacks on finality oooh ok i see, yes thanks for clarifying that. but then what about 16 slots per epoch? all validators would attest during that epoch. mh I immagine that the 32 slots per epoch is to be safe everyone attests once per epoch at least then fix on my statement: there are actually 1m validators active so yeah i think that answers my own question

excerpts.content: Does anyone know when the next spec test release will be?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the next one would be `alpha.7`, and we are working on getting that together

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: a few key PRs are still in progress

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: curiosity: right now on the network we have 64 committees each consisted of 526 validator. this means that we are aggregating (supposedly) 33664 attestations per slot. correct? if so why not bump down epoch duration to `8` slots? is it the computation or is there something else i am missing? for that specific epoch with an `8` slots duration you would get `33664*8=269312` which is almost half the current active validator set length

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
64 committees per slot, and yes each committee has something like 526 validators

so then 33664 attestations/slot

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: if epochs were shorter, we would have even more attestations/slot to aggregate

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: which is in general one of the more expensive computations we have in the CL

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: there's also the trade-off b/t per-slot, per-block, and per-epoch scope processing nodes have to do; if epochs are shorter you get less amortization

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
> for that specific epoch with an 8 slots duration you would get 33664*8=269312 which is almost half the current active validator set length 
i think you are starting at the other end of the design space here -- we want the invariant that every validator makes 1 attestation per epoch; otherwise you start getting much more complicated analyses around finality/PoS security

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: which at best is harder to secure, and at worst means we open ourselves up to attacks on finality

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: oooh ok i see, yes thanks for clarifying that. but then what about 16 slots per epoch? all validators would attest during that epoch. mh I immagine that the 32 slots per epoch is to be safe everyone attests once per epoch at least then

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: fix on my statement: there are actually 1m validators active so yeah i think that answers my own question
